text:
St. Louis honoured Keith Tkachuk before the game, and he dropped the ceremonial puck between his two sons, both now wearing Panthers sweaters. Then the sons went to work on his old team. Brady Tkachuk scored on a first-period power play, set up by Sam Reinhart and Matthew, and Florida won 4-1 for its third straight win.

The Panthers took the game in the first 25 minutes. Brady's goal came at 5:12, and 77 seconds later Dmitry Kulikov scored on a slap shot that goes in about 1% of the time. Anton Lundell made it 3-0 early in the second off a Brady Tkachuk pass, which pushed Florida's win chance past 90%. Reinhart's goal at 7:38 of the third was his 700th career point, a fitting number for a player the Panthers' own channel is now asking about in Hall of Fame terms.

The result flatters Florida a bit. St. Louis had more of the chances overall (3.24 expected goals to 2.67, the quality of looks each side got) and dominated the third period, 1.97 to 0.72, once the game was out of reach. The Blues won this one in 60% of our replays of every shot. What stood in the way was Jacob Markstrom, who stopped 23 of 24 and saved 2.2 goals more than those shots usually allow. Dylan Holloway finally beat him on a power play with 2:06 left. Joel Hofer, two nights after a shutout of Utah, allowed four on 28.

Matthew Tkachuk didn't score, missing the net on the best chance of the night (37%), but his assist kept his point streak going and leaves him one shy of 700 for his career. Florida did all of this without Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand, both reported as close to returning. The Panthers go to Dallas tonight on the second half of a back-to-back.
headline: On Keith Tkachuk's night, his sons run the show
